requirements.text: Change the background into a basketball court
requirements.source_phrase: Change the background into a basketball court

outcomes.description: Replace the image background with a basketball court.
outcomes.target: The background is visibly a basketball court, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the requested background change in R1.

nodes.question: Does the edited image show the background changed into a basketball court?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the background as a whole is recognizably a basketball court, based on the visible scene in context. A playing surface and court markings are useful evidence, but no single feature is mandatory; basketball equipment alone does not establish a court. Fail if the background is clearly not recognizable as a basketball court. Unknown if the visual evidence does not reliably settle whether the background reads as a court.
nodes.binding: Judge completion of the requested background replacement, not merely the presence of basketball-related objects. Assess the background as a whole and weigh visible court surface, markings, equipment, and surrounding context together. Do not require any unsupported specific feature or force a conclusion at an ambiguous threshold.

nodes.question: Is there visible evidence that the background has begun changing toward a basketball court, even though completion is not established by this check?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows discernible progress toward replacing the background with a basketball court, including basketball-related scene changes or partial court cues. Fail if there is no visible progress toward that requested background change. Unknown if progress cannot be distinguished from the original or assessed reliably. This is a progress judgment, not a completion judgment; a complete court background may also pass.
nodes.binding: Assess only progress toward the requested background replacement. Do not use this check to decide whether the background is complete; unrelated edits do not count as progress.

nodes.question: Replace the image background with a basketball court.
nodes.criteria: Return complete if s1 passes. Otherwise, return absent only if s1 fails and s2 fails, establishing no requested progress. Return partial if s1 fails and s2 passes, establishing incomplete progress toward the court background. Return unknown if evidence needed to distinguish these outcomes is unresolved, including when s1 is unknown and completion cannot be established. A pass on s2 does not establish completion, and unrelated edits do not count.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

fulfillment: The node’s criteria make the aggregate label partial whenever s1 fails and s2 passes, and the trace follows that rule. Yet the edited image visibly includes a court surface and court markings, as well as a hoop and basketballs; the s1 failure appears to hinge on an overly narrow or inconsistent interpretation of what establishes a recognizable court background. Refine the binding and s1 evidence standard to assess the whole background and accept these visible court features together, rather than treating the dark upper backdrop alone as decisive. Keep s2 as evidence of progress, not completion by itself, and retain the distinction between complete, partial, absent, and unresolved. The trace is valid and queried, with no transport or schema failure; the disagreement is visual/criterion interpretation, not a reason to force the reference label.
s2: The s2 trace is valid and correctly identifies progress, but the aggregate remains partial because s1 appears to apply an overly narrow completion standard. Improve the executable node’s binding or typed criteria so completion is judged from the entire visible background, not just the dark upper backdrop: the edited image shows a basketball hoop and ball, court floor, and court markings together. Keep s2 limited to progress and preserve the distinction between complete, partial, absent, and unresolved; do not force completion from s2 alone or treat low confidence as evidence of missing edits. The trace has no transport, schema, or dependency failure, so target the visual completion criterion rather than execution plumbing.
s1: The binding is already appropriately scoped to judge the background as a whole, so avoid broadening it or lowering the completion threshold just to match the reference label. The trace’s claim that no court surface or markings are visible conflicts with the edited image: a playing surface and court lines are clearly visible across the lower background, alongside the hoop and basketballs. Improve the node’s evidence assessment so it considers the full image rather than letting the dark upper backdrop outweigh those visible court cues; require the scene to read as a court overall, not merely contain basketball equipment. Preserve partial versus complete and unresolved distinctions, and do not treat the reference label as atomic ground truth. This is a visual-evidence/criterion-application issue, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure.

transaction.reason: The broad court-feature check passes on the hoop and marked floor, but that does not by itself establish that the background has been changed into a court. Add a targeted completion check for whether the visible background reads as a court beyond isolated equipment and a narrow strip of floor. Keep the existing progress check and do not treat the image-grounded hypothesis as an atomic answer.

actions.question: Beyond basketball equipment and a limited strip of marked floor, does the visible background establish a basketball-court setting?
actions.criteria: Pass if the visible background as a whole is recognizably a basketball court, with enough court surface or surrounding court context to establish the requested background replacement. Fail if the court identity is conveyed only by isolated basketball equipment or a small amount of court surface while the remaining background is not recognizably a court. Unknown if the visible background does not permit a reliable judgment.
actions.binding: Assess whether the edited background fulfills the request to change the background into a basketball court. Use the source image only as context for the requested replacement; do not infer completion from basketball props alone.

actions.criteria: Return complete only if s1 passes and s1a passes, establishing both recognizable court features and a sufficiently established court background. If completion is not established, return partial when s2 passes, since it indicates requested progress; return absent only when s2 fails and the evidence establishes no requested progress. Return unknown when the evidence needed to distinguish these outcomes is unresolved. A pass on s1 alone does not establish completion, and unrelated edits do not count.

semantic_rejection.reason: The chain makes s1, s1a, and s2 all required for fulfillment, so an unknown or skipped progress check can block a complete result even when s1 and s1a establish completion. It also makes s1a a required completion condition, although the original rubric requires only that the requested change be complete; the extra whole-background test can reject a visibly completed court background based on an unsupported interpretation.
semantic_rejection.source_clause: yes means all requested changes are complete
semantic_rejection.counterexample: The edited image visibly has a basketball-court background with recognizable court features, so the requested change is complete, but s1a fails because the background is judged not to read as a coherent court setting, or s2 is unknown/skipped. Fulfillment cannot return complete because all three checks are required, despite the original rubric's completion criterion being met.
